_handoff.scope: Public first-person accounts about Karnataka Kaveri marriage registration used from Bengaluru only. They expose possible portal and review friction; they are not statutory eligibility, current SRO policy, document requirements, fees, or service-level commitments. Names, usernames, relationship details, addresses, application identifiers, contact information, and other personal data are intentionally omitted.

sources.title: Marriage Certificate at Kaveri Portal - My Experience
sources.notes: The post and comments contain several first-person Kaveri experiences, including a reported digitally signed certificate, objections, repeated e-sign/OTP activity and a payment-status anomaly. Each is anecdotal; no stated format, payment, route, timing or SRO practice is retained as a general requirement.

claims.text: One citizen reported receiving a digitally signed marriage certificate through the Kaveri portal without describing an in-person visit.
claims.notes: One reported success. It does not establish eligibility, legal route, online availability for every SRO, or a completion time.

claims.text: One citizen reported that an objection after submission required the couple and witnesses to repeat Aadhaar-based verification and e-sign steps.
claims.notes: A single report of a post-objection workflow outcome. It does not prove that all objections reset verification or identify the cause of an objection.

claims.text: A commenter reported receiving a failed-payment acknowledgement but later receiving an SMS that the marriage certificate was ready.
claims.notes: One reported interface/status discrepancy, not proof that a payment failed, that a certificate was valid, or that waiting resolves another case.

claims.text: The citizen accounts do not establish which legal route, SRO, document set, verification sequence, payment amount, or certificate outcome applies to a particular marriage-registration case.
claims.notes: No login, OTP, form, upload, payment, appointment or submission was attempted.

roadblocks.title: Reported objection may require repeated participation
roadblocks.symptom: A citizen reports having to repeat verification and e-sign activity after an objection.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Unknown; the account does not verify the objection reason or whether the reset is universal.
roadblocks.recovery: Treat this as a coordination risk only: obtain the authorised case-specific objection reason and follow the portal/SRO's current instructions rather than relying on anecdotal steps.

roadblocks.title: Reported portal payment/status ambiguity
roadblocks.symptom: A commenter describes a payment acknowledgement that appeared unsuccessful followed by a readiness message.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Unknown; no transaction or case state was independently inspected.
roadblocks.recovery: Keep authorised transaction and case references, and use the current official portal or SRO support route to reconcile a real discrepancy. Do not repeat a payment solely on this anecdote.
